candidates.clause_text: The restriction applies to all liability coverages, classifications, locations, and operations scheduled on the issued policy. Coverage does not apply to any bodily injury or property damage arising out of the actual, alleged, or threatened presence of silica. The exclusion equally applies to personal and advertising injury claims stemming from the distribution, sale, handling, or inhalation of such materials. For the purposes of this endorsement, silica is defined as silicon dioxide occurring in crystalline, amorphous, or impure forms, including sand and quartz. Silica-related dust is defined as a mixture or combination of silica and other dust particles that may become airborne during business operations.

The carrier bears no obligation to provide indemnification for any loss, cost, settlement, or expense related to the specified mineral compounds. Furthermore, the carrier assumes no responsibility to defend any suit, action, or proceeding seeking damages attributable to silica or silica-related dust. The restriction extends to any discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release, or escape of the dust into the environment or indoor workspaces. Coverage is excluded whether the introduction of the dust was sudden, accidental, gradual, or occurred over an extended period of time. No coverage is provided for any request, demand, order, or statutory requirement that any insured or others test for or monitor the dust.

Similarly, costs associated with cleaning up, removing, containing, treating, detoxifying, or neutralizing the specified mineral dust are entirely excluded from this policy. Claims made by or on behalf of any governmental authority for damages resulting from testing, monitoring, or remediation are also excluded. Any product, material, or good manufactured, sold, handled, distributed, or disposed of by the insured containing these minerals falls under this restriction. Liability assumed under any contract or agreement regarding the remediation or containment of these dust particles is similarly excluded from coverage.

The restriction applies to operations conducted at scheduled premises, temporary worksites, and all products and completed operations hazards involving the specified dust. If any portion of a claim involves allegations both related and unrelated to the excluded dust, the carrier will not allocate defense costs. Instead, the entire claim shall be deemed excluded if the primary or underlying allegation stems from the presence of the specified minerals. Insureds are expected to maintain accurate records of materials used in their manufacturing, construction, or contracting processes to verify compliance. Failure on the part of the insured to identify the presence of these minerals in raw materials does not invalidate this exclusion.

The carrier reserves the right to deny indemnification for any settlement reached without prior written consent regarding these specific mineral liabilities. This exclusion applies to all exposure bases, including gross sales, payroll, area, and cost of work, regardless of premium calculation methods. Any exception to pollution exclusions found elsewhere in the policy documentation does not apply to the mineral compounds defined herein. The provisions set forth in this endorsement are absolute and apply to all operations, classifications, and territories associated with the insured business. In the event that any court or jurisdiction finds a portion of this exclusion unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain in full effect.

Damages encompass statutory fines, penalties, punitive assessments, and multiplied damages levied by governmental bodies or regulatory agencies concerning the excluded dust. The exclusion applies regardless of whether the dust was introduced into the environment by the named insured or by any third party. No coverage exceptions apply for the completed operations hazard or the products hazard when the underlying injury involves the specified mineral compounds. This endorsement controls over any conflicting provisions in the coverage part and applies consistently across all scheduled limits and classifications.
